opener: Father, I keep opening my life next to everyone else's and grading mine lower.
paragraphs: I scroll a feed built to show me the best five seconds of someone else's whole year, and I let it testify about my entire life. Their new house, her new ring, his launch, her body, their calm — and I come away convinced I'm behind in a race You never actually asked me to run. I've held my rough draft up against everyone else's highlight reel and called the verdict honest, when it was really just comparison wearing the costume of humility.

So free me from a scoreboard You never built, Lord. Let me measure my life by what You've placed inside it, not by what I can see lit up in someone else's. You are finishing my story exactly on time — not behind, not late, not forgotten at the back of a line while everyone else moves up. Close the gap between what I have and what I think I should have by now, and give me eyes that can celebrate someone else's harvest without starving over my own. In Jesus' name, amen.
bold: You are finishing my story exactly on time
kicker: A Prayer For When Comparison Won't Quit
